stem: Select all TRUE statements about the EstimatorV2 `resilience_level` option.

options.text: Level 1 is the default and applies readout-error mitigation (TREX).
Higher resilience levels typically reduce total runtime, because fewer circuits are executed.
Level 2 additionally applies zero-noise extrapolation (on top of level 1).
Setting `resilience_level = 3` turns on probabilistic error cancellation (PEC).
Options you set explicitly are applied on top of the base settings a resilience level defines.

explanation.correct: The resilience level is a coarse cost/accuracy dial: level 0 = no mitigation, level 1 (the default) = readout-error mitigation via TREX, and level 2 = level 1 plus zero-noise extrapolation and gate twirling. Higher levels give more accurate (less biased) results at greater cost. A resilience level is only a base set of options: anything you set yourself (for example turning measurement mitigation back off at level 1) is applied in addition to it.

distractors.C: Higher levels run MORE circuits (an ensemble for mitigation) and take longer, not less — they trade runtime for accuracy.
distractors.E: Level 3 does not exist for EstimatorV2 — the supported choices are 0, 1 and 2, and setting 3 raises a validation error. PEC is reached through the individual option `resilience.pec_mitigation`, not through a resilience level.

provenance.notes: adversarial s6: hedge added to distractor C (hedge tell); E replaced with the plausible 'level 3 = PEC' misconception | added true option F (explicit options layer on top of the resilience level) so the section's multi-selects no longer all have exactly 3 correct answers
